structuredReview.summary: Four blockers and two non-blocking verification gaps remain.

findings.title: The Vite+ runner test bypasses the consumer-facing composite
findings.trigger: setup-webpresso-toolchain later passes an explicit version, uses the wrong working directory, or otherwise changes its setup-vp invocation while the qualification continues invoking voidzero-dev/setup-vp directly.
findings.impact: The runner qualification remains green even though consumers of the repository's public composite no longer receive manifest or catalog resolution.
findings.fix: Run the fixture matrix through the local setup-webpresso-toolchain action, and have the parsed contract assert its embedded setup-vp SHA, run-install setting, working-directory behavior, and absence of a version override.

findings.title: The second cache pass can succeed without exercising cache-hit setup
findings.trigger: The second setup-wp invocation becomes a no-op or returns before adding the cached tool to PATH; the first invocation's GITHUB_PATH entry still lets the later wp command succeed.
findings.impact: All stated assertions can pass while setup-wp's cache-hit path is broken, so the claimed miss-to-hit behavior is not proven.
findings.fix: Remove or isolate the first pass's PATH effect before the second invocation and assert that the second invocation itself re-exports the exact cached executable path or emits an equivalent cache-hit signal.

findings.title: No successful hosted-runner execution is an explicit delivery gate
findings.trigger: Local ci-act prerequisites are unavailable and only bun tests plus actionlint run before delivery.
findings.impact: The plan can complete without executing either new qualification on a GitHub-hosted runner, leaving both external behavior claims unverified.
findings.fix: Require a successful hosted self-test run covering both qualification jobs, with a run URL or equivalent receipt; keep ci-act as optional supplemental evidence.

findings.title: Immutable-reference acceptance conflicts with required local action usage
findings.location: Task 99.3 acceptance: all changed action references
findings.trigger: Task 99.2 adds or changes uses: ./.github/actions/setup-wp as required.
findings.impact: That local action reference cannot be a full immutable SHA, so the acceptance criteria are internally impossible to satisfy literally.
findings.fix: Limit the SHA requirement to changed remote action references and explicitly permit repository-local action paths.

findings.title: Interrupted cache seeding is not covered
findings.trigger: The first invocation is cancelled after creating the version directory but before installing a usable executable.
findings.impact: A partial cache entry could be mistaken for a hit on a later run; the planned two successful passes would not expose this case.
findings.fix: Add a partial-cache or interrupted-seed case that must be rejected, cleaned, or safely reseeded.

findings.title: Resolution error behavior is not qualified
findings.trigger: A manifest references a missing catalog name or the lockfile lacks a matching Vite+ entry.
findings.impact: The action could silently fall back or produce an unclear failure without detection by the two valid-fixture cases.
findings.fix: Add one malformed or unresolved fixture and assert a nonzero, diagnostic failure with no latest-version fallback.

structuredReview.summary: 4 prior findings are fixed, 2 are still open, and 0 are not a blocker. gate:04344b598ab9257d:codex:gpt-5.6-sol#1 is fixed: Task 99.1 invokes the local consumer composite and binds its SHA, run-install, version, and working-directory contract. #2 is still open: Task 99.2 resets PATH but neither clears runner-managed GITHUB_PATH state nor resets the first pass's WP_INSTALL_DIR. #3 is fixed by the mandatory hosted Self-test receipt. #4 is fixed by limiting SHA enforcement to remote references. #5 is fixed by the non-executable partial-cache fixture and required reseed. #6 is still open as a nit because the missing-catalog case asserts failure but no diagnostic. Dimension review: (1) the remaining cache-isolation blocker makes the stated proof internally unsound; (2) no blocker; (3) the same blocker plus two test-completeness nits; (4) the same blocker and diagnostic/usability nits; (5) no blocker; (6) no additional blocker.

findings.title: The second cache pass can succeed without exercising cache-hit setup
findings.location: Task 99.2, second-pass acceptance and Material Decision D2
findings.trigger: The first composite writes its cache directory to GITHUB_PATH and WP_INSTALL_DIR through GitHub file commands, then the second composite is a no-op. Runner-managed GITHUB_PATH entries are reapplied to later steps, and the first WP_INSTALL_DIR remains available, so merely restoring a captured PATH does not reliably remove either first-pass signal.
findings.impact: Both post-second-pass assertions can still reflect the first invocation, allowing the qualification to pass while setup-wp's cache-hit path is broken.
findings.fix: Require a step-scoped cache-hit/install-directory output from the second action and assert that output, or run the second invocation in a genuinely fresh hosted job after transferring the seeded cache in a permission-preserving archive. If ambient variables remain part of the proof, explicitly clear WP_INSTALL_DIR as well.

findings.title: Resolution error behavior is not qualified
findings.trigger: The missing catalog makes the composite fail with an unrelated or opaque error rather than a catalog-resolution diagnostic.
findings.impact: The outcome assertion passes without establishing that users receive a meaningful resolution failure.
findings.fix: Assert a stable catalog-resolution error marker or error category in addition to the failed step outcome.

findings.title: Valid resolution fixtures may accidentally agree with the default version
findings.trigger: A fixture's lockfile-pinned expected version equals setup-vp's default or current latest version, and the action ignores the manifest or named catalog.
findings.impact: The valid cases can pass without proving either requested resolution path; the missing-catalog case only excludes fallback on its own error path.
findings.fix: Require valid fixtures to pin deliberately non-default versions, preferably distinct versions for the range and catalog cases.

findings.title: The cache qualification does not execute the installed binary
findings.trigger: The cache path contains an executable but corrupt, wrong-architecture, or wrong-version wp file.
findings.impact: Executable-bit, WP_INSTALL_DIR, and command-resolution checks pass even though the claimed tool installation is unusable or nondeterministic.
findings.fix: Execute the exact cached binary after seeding and after the isolated hit, asserting its expected version.

structuredReview.summary: 3 prior findings fixed, 1 still open, 0 not a blocker. Adjudications: gate:a8821cb979d66f28:codex:gpt-5.6-sol#1 is fixed because Task 99.2 requires artifact-only transfer into a separate fresh hosted job. #2 is still open because Task 99.1 only emits “unresolved-named-catalog rejected” after observing any composite failure; it does not assert the composite’s underlying catalog-resolution diagnostic. #3 is fixed because Task 99.1 specifies distinct, deliberate non-default versions 0.1.0 and 0.1.1. #4 is fixed because both cache jobs execute the exact cached binary with --help. Dimension review: (1) no blocker; (2) no blocker; (3) no blocker, with the diagnostic-assertion nit below; (4) no blocker, with the same failure-path nit; (5) no blocker; (6) no blocker.

findings.title: Resolution error behavior is not qualified
findings.trigger: The local composite fails for malformed fixture YAML, an unavailable dependency, or another unrelated setup error; the following assertion then emits the plan-owned “unresolved-named-catalog rejected” marker solely because the outcome was failure.
findings.impact: The workflow can pass without proving that a missing named catalog is the reason for rejection or that users receive a recognizable resolution diagnostic.
findings.fix: Capture the failing composite’s output or log and assert a stable catalog-resolution error marker or error category before emitting the workflow marker.
